records.title: Welcome to the official Instagram account of @lawyer_oyer ‘s new podcast. Is This Really Legal? is available at the link in our bio or wherever you get your podcasts.

This week, Liz talks with Lucius T. Outlaw III, an associate professor of law at Howard University School of Law and former federal public defender, about how grand juries work, what standard of proof applies, and why their proceedings are secret.

Give Is This Really Legal? a listen wherever you get your podcasts.

What made retired Navy Commander Bobby Jones start to change his mind on the role of civilian courts on military issues? Give our most recent episode a listen and let us know what you think.

Is This Really Legal? is available wherever you get your podcasts.

Liz talks with retired Navy Commander Bobby Jones about the 200-plus consecutive days the crew of the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln has spent at sea without a port call — and why service members have almost no legal recourse even when conditions are bad.

Give it a listen wherever you get your podcasts!

Liz Oyer takes you on an inside tour of the Department of Justice. To understand what’s happening in the country—and why it matters—you need to understand how DOJ actually works.

Stay tuned for part two or watch the whole video on YouTube now (link in bio).

"Is This Really Legal?" answers real questions about government power, in plain English. No law degree required.

Your host, @lawyer_oyer, is a former public defender and former Pardon Attorney at the U.S. Department of Justice, where she served under both Democratic and Republican presidents.

Follow along, and send us the questions you want answered.

Stephen Richer, former Recorder of Maricopa County, explains how Americans across the country have embraced the accessibility and convenience of mail ballots while ensuring that improvements are made to secure mail voting.

If you have questions about election administration, let us know in the comments below.

This week, Liz is joined by Stephen Richer, former Recorder of Maricopa County, to break down the reality of how elections are administered in the United States. Give it a listen wherever you get your podcasts!

Do you have questions about election administration? Let us know in the comments.

If you saw The Odyssey this weekend, you might want to hear Bill Baer and Liz discuss the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger and how it could affect American consumers. 

Is This Really Legal? is available wherever you get your podcasts.

This week, @lawyer_oyer is joined by Bill Baer, who led antitrust enforcement at both the DOJ and FTC, for a candid, funny, and timely conversation about antitrust law. Give it a listen wherever you get your podcasts, and if you learned something new from the episode, let us know what it was below.

"We're done with this Epstein name. We're calling you guys the Golden Warriors now."

Advocate Dani Bensky tells Liz some of the names her fellow survivors have brainstormed for themselves instead of "Epstein victims." Leave any suggestions you have in the comments!

This week's episode if Is This Really Legal? is available wherever you get your podcasts.

We're lucky to have been joined this week by Dani Bensky, an artist, advocate, and survivor of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse. She joins Liz to discuss her experience testifying at Todd Blanche's confirmation hearing and how being a survivor shapes her advocacy and her art. Available wherever you get your podcasts.

New York Times reporter Devlin Barrett, who has covered law enforcement for more than 20 years, joins Liz to talk about how the Epstein files might feature in Todd Blanche's upcoming confirmation hearing. 

Watch the new episode of Is This Really Legal? at the link in our bio.
What happens in private meetings between nominees and senators? Find out on the most recent episode of Is This Really Legal? at the link in our bio.

"It's a really bad way to get to the truth," says former Senate Judiciary Committee counsel Gregg Nunziata on why the five-minute questioning format fails at confirmation hearings.

Watch the full episode of Is This Really Legal? at the link in our bio.

It was just reported that Donald Trump made over $2 billion during the first year of his presidency. My friend @katiecouric asked me: Is this really legal? Watch and subscribe to @isthisreallylegal for answers. Thanks for the great question, Katie, and keep them coming, everyone!
"If you don't think a crime has been committed, then full stop," says former Acting AG Peter Keisler. Watch the full episode of Is This Really Legal? at the link in our bio.

@lawyer_oyer wants to answer your questions on her show! Send us an email or leave a message with your questions about the justice system, the courts, or anything else in the legal news. Contact info is available at link in bio, and follow Is This Really Legal? for new episodes on Thursdays.

For our inaugural episode, former Acting AG Peter Keisler sits down with Liz to guide listeners on a tour of the Department of Justice. 

The first episode of Is This Really Legal? is live at the link in our bio.

Can the president prosecute his enemies? In a sneak peek of our first episode, former DOJ Pardon Attorney Liz Oyer breaks it down with former Acting Attorney General Peter Keisler. Tune in tomorrow for their full conversation.
